themes_detail.label: Building Code Violations Surge
themes_detail.summary: Building/Use complaints spiked to 16 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.9 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 753% increase (z-score: 10.36)—suggesting a sudden cluster of code enforcement issues or illegal occupancy/conversion activity in Greenwich Village/SoHo.
evidence: 16 Building/Use complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (753% spike, z-score 10.36)
1,175 alteration permits filed in last 90 days (by far the dominant DOB filing type), suggesting widespread renovation activity that may be outpacing inspection capacity
Community Board has repeatedly requested enhanced housing inspection programs (annual budget request), indicating chronic code violation issues
reporting_angles: Are landlords converting residential units without permits or illegally subdividing apartments in a post-pandemic rush to maximize occupancy?
Is DOB inspection capacity keeping pace with the 1,175+ alterations filed in 90 days—and are violations being caught or ignored?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Spike
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints jumped to 19 THIS WEEK versus a 4.1 per-week baseline—a 361% spike (z-score: 8.44)—indicating a sudden waste disposal problem in the district, likely tied to construction debris from ongoing alterations or commercial operations.
evidence: 19 illegal dumping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (361% increase, z-score 8.44)
1,327 DOB permits filed in last 90 days (1,175 alterations alone), generating construction debris and potential improper disposal
Community Board has repeatedly requested increased sanitation trucks and equipment (annual budget request), suggesting chronic capacity gaps
reporting_angles: Are construction projects from the 1,175+ active alterations disposing of debris improperly or overwhelming legal disposal sites?
Is DSNY adequately monitoring and enforcing against dumping in a high-development district, or are fines too weak to deter repeat offenders?

themes_detail.label: Street Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints surged to 61 THIS WEEK versus a 18.6 per-week baseline—a 228% spike (z-score: 6.12)—coinciding with the graffiti and illegal dumping spikes, suggesting potential environmental neglect or construction damage across the district.
evidence: 61 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 18.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (228% increase, z-score 6.12)
Concurrent spikes in graffiti (49 complaints 2 weeks ago, up 494%) and illegal dumping (19 this week, up 361%) suggest district-wide deterioration
Community Board repeatedly requests catch basin cleaning and street tree maintenance (annual budget requests), indicating chronic infrastructure gaps
reporting_angles: Are construction projects damaging streets and sidewalks faster than DOT can repair them?
Are reduced street sweeping and maintenance in the district contributing to accumulating debris and graffiti?

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Wave (2 weeks old)
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints peaked at 49 TWO WEEKS AGO versus a 8.2 per-week baseline—a 494% spike (z-score: 7.15)—indicating a potential tagging campaign or enforcement lag in a high-profile commercial/cultural district.
evidence: 49 graffiti complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 8.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (494% increase, z-score 7.15)
Spike predates current illegal dumping and street condition surges, but may be related to broader environmental neglect
Community Board has requested Argus surveillance cameras (annual budget request), signaling frustration with repeat vandalism
reporting_angles: Is a specific tagging crew responsible, or is this evidence of reduced NYPD/Sanitation enforcement?
Would increased surveillance cameras (as CB annually requests) deter repeat offenders or is the issue resource allocation?

themes_detail.label: Animal Abuse Reports (last week)
themes_detail.summary: Animal abuse complaints spiked to 9 LAST WEEK versus a 1.6 per-week baseline—a 454% increase (z-score: 7.43)—a notable but isolated signal potentially tied to seasonal factors or a specific incident cluster.
evidence: 9 animal abuse complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (454% increase, z-score 7.43)
Spike is isolated to one week and does not correlate with other district-wide deterioration signals
Community Board requests public health programs (annual budget request), though animal welfare is not explicitly mentioned
reporting_angles: Was there a specific incident or location cluster that drove the spike, or does this reflect a chronic enforcement issue?
Are animal control resources adequate in a dense commercial/residential district with high foot traffic and outdoor dining?
